tldr: This slug used to track speculative decoding; after reclustering it holds 35 unrelated arXiv papers from Nov 9 onward whose only link is "Large Language Models" in the title. Read it as a research digest: most papers question how LLMs are evaluated, measure hallucination and uncertainty, or probe safety, with a few on infra such as LM-SimBench and MemOnce.
whats_new: Two more benchmarks landed Nov 25: Merlin-Bench finds 10 frontier LLMs struggle to produce proofs a formal verifier accepts, and VulnSafe scores eight models on 2,050 Chinese relational-safety prompts.
why_it_matters: There is no single event here. The useful signal is that eval methodology itself keeps getting challenged (shifting human raters, adaptive users, unvalidated user simulators), which is the layer your agent eval harness depends on.

beats.headline: LLMs applied to AutoML, fault diagnosis, anomaly detection and program induction
beats.summary: Domain papers that use an LLM as a component; little here touches serving or agent infrastructure.

beats.headline: Papers question whether LLM evaluations measure what they claim
beats.summary: Human raters getting stricter, users adapting mid-conversation, unvalidated user simulators and name-only knowledge probes each can skew a score.

beats.headline: Uncertainty, abstention and decoding-time fixes for hallucination
beats.summary: Black-box uncertainty estimates, calibrated abstention thresholds, deception probes, and training-free multimodal decoding fixes, capped by a 116-paper survey.

beats.headline: Framing attacks, jailbreak detection, malware triage and quantization backdoors
beats.summary: Security-side papers: how headline framing sways model judgments, detecting jailbreaks without an extra classifier, and repairing backdoors that only fire after quantization.

beats.headline: Training simulators, memory-compressed long context and population-based RL
beats.summary: The platform-relevant slice: LM-SimBench for parallelism simulators, a survey of LLMs for AI infra, MemOnce's compact KV memory, and RL post-training methods for agents.

beats.headline: Merlin-Bench and VulnSafe add verifier-checked proofs and relational safety

open_questions: Does MemOnce's reported 1313x smaller memory cache at 1M context hold up in an independent reproduction or open serving stack?
Do other labs adopt Merlin-Bench's verifier-checked proof protocol for agent evals?
Does the "raters got pickier" finding change how ChatGPT-style regressions are reported or re-tested?
Will reclustering pull speculative-decoding papers back into this slug, or does it stay a generic LLM-research grab-bag?
take_for_builders: If your agent evals rely on a user simulator or LLM-as-judge, validate it against a small human-labeled set before trusting a week-over-week regression signal.
